newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada premier's son arrested on assault charges.
newsitem.headline: Canada premier's son arrested on assault charges.

text.p: The adopted son of Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien was arrested this week for violating a court order to stay away from a woman and child he was charged with assaulting, police said on Thursday.
Regina Police Sgt. Hal Zorn said Michel Chretien, 28, was arrested on Feb. 25 on assault charges against a 37-year-old woman and her seven-year-old son.
Zorn said that after Chretien was arraigned in February, he was released on condition he not contact the woman or the boy except through a lawyer, police or social workers.
Chretien was arrested again on Tuesday after a citizen complained to police that he took the woman and boy on a social outing, Zorn said.
News of the assault charges were not reported until Thursday.
Chretien has been released pending a court appearance on July 7. He was released from a Regina halfway house on Feb. 14 after serving two-thirds of a three-year sentence for sexual assault.
Chretien was adopted by the prime minister from an Arctic orphanage in the 1970s when his adoptive father was Minister of Indian Affairs.
The elder Chretien is campaigning for re-election in the June 2 federal election.
